keyFindings: VERDICT: the strong hypothesis is REFUTED. Drift does NOT near-vanish for female investigators: the three Eleanor-led stories carry 14, 23, and 26 sentence-level drift instances (vs 26 for the Hugo-led story), and Eleanor herself is misgendered as he/his/him 5-10 times per story — a 'female-investigator prior' cannot produce masculine pronouns on a female investigator.

A weaker form of the hypothesis survives: investigator-DIRECTED drift is ~3x higher when the investigator is male (Hugo 21 instances, 100% feminine-direction, vs Eleanor mean 7), so a male investigator does attract disproportionate she/her narration. But the S1 cast is 5-of-6 female (Eleanor victim, Mallory, Beatrice, Sylvia, plus male Hale), so majority-gender pressure explains this as well as an Eleanor-investigator prior does.

The single largest drift target across all four stories is Captain Ivor Hale — 33 instances, all male->feminine, and he is NEVER the investigator. His feminizations cluster (a) in interrogation scenes opposite female Eleanor and (b) in recurring trait-template sentences: 'She adjusted her watch chain / her navy suit / her thin leather belt' recurs with feminine pronouns in S3 chapters 3, 4, 7, and 8. Drift attaches to trait-phrase templates and to whoever shares scenes with opposite-gender characters, not to the investigator role per se.

Mechanism signature is interlocutor/nearest-referent gender bleed, bidirectional within the same exchange: S4 ch2 'He steadied himself, smoothing the sleeve of his wool skirt, and turned to face Captain Ivor Hale' (female Eleanor masculinized while facing a man, garment stays female); S3 ch1 'Her voice... faltered as she addressed Eleanor. Is there any hope? he asked' (male Hale feminized while addressing a woman, flipping back mid-passage).

Antecedent distances are tiny and repair-friendly: in ~80% of instances the correct name is 0-2 sentences away, and passages frequently flip back to the correct gender in the next clause or dialogue tag — this is exactly the pattern the Item 13 detector/repair layer (documentation/analysis/ANALYSIS_62/ITEM_13_PRONOUN_DRIFT_SPEC.md, fix commit 047d469f) should catch, yet both 2026-07-22 probe runs (post-fix) still ship 26 and 14 instances.

Template/duplication carrier: the drifted sentence 'He pressed his fingers to his temple, recalling Hugo Vane's last words to him' appears VERBATIM in S3 ch1 and ch10 — wrong-gender pronouns are being propagated by repeated obligation/summary boilerplate, consistent with the known agent9 post-processing/template layer (see memory: post-LLM passes corrupt clean output).

Drift is NOT investigator-specific: in the female-investigator stories 64-74% of drift lands on non-investigator MALE characters (Hale, Hugo). The reviewer's 'role-pronoun contamination toward a female-investigator prior' fits only the S1 investigator subset; the cross-story data better fits character-agnostic referent confusion biased toward the locally dominant gender (feminine direction = 67% overall, matching the heavily female casts).

Secondary observations: S4 has an ungendered minor character (forensic tech) whose pronouns cycle he->she->him within one passage (ch6), and S1's male investigator drift persists into pure introspection with no female character in the sentence (ch10 'She felt the ache of her own failure'), i.e. once drifted, a passage can stay drifted for 2-3 sentences before snapping back.
